extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark composed of 680 question-answer pairs from four real-world domains (conference, organization, education, and game) across over 1373 webpages, designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to traverse websites' subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. It includes both single-source and multi-source QA types in English and Chinese.
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang (Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy was employed, combining LLM-based and human annotation. In the first stage, GPT-4o performs initial annotations by traversing official websites recursively, constructing queries, and filtering QA pairs. In the second stage, crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering to refine the final results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains, collected by systematically clicking and collecting subpages accessible through sublinks on the root page.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries are verified and filtered for legitimate queries that deviate from natural, human-like phrasing, retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: GPT-4o performs initial LLM-based annotation to generate synthetic QA pairs from collected web page information. Human annotators then rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure the QA pairs are correct and consistent.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Even the best-performing WebWalker using GPT-4o as its backbone does not surpass 40% accuracy. WebWalkerQA is built on official websites with dynamically updated information, while pre-trained models rely on static knowledge limited by a cutoff date.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of LLMs on web traversal tasks, testing RAG systems' ability to retrieve deep information from websites, and evaluating multi-step information-seeking capabilities.

name.evidence: We introduce WebWalkerQA, a benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal.

description.evidence: We construct a challenging benchmark, WebWalkerQA, which is composed of 680 queries from four real-world scenarios across over 1373 webpages.

creator.evidence: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group

inLanguage.evidence: WebWalkerQA is a bilingual dataset that includes both Chinese and English, reflecting the most widely used and universal languages in real-world web environments.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: To make the annotation process cost-efficient and accurate, we employ a two-stage funnel annotation strategy, combining LLM-based and human annotation. In the first stage, GPT-4o (OpenAI, 2022b), performs initial annotations, followed by a second stage, where crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering to refine the final results.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Step1: Traverse official websites recursively, collecting information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages... followed by a second stage, where crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control and filtering to refine the final results.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We first collect root official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains. Then we mimic human behavior by systematically clicking and collecting subpages accessible through sublinks on the root page.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Step3: Verify and filter for legitimate queries that deviate from natural, human-like phrasing, retaining only QA pairs with short answers containing entities.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Using predefined rules, we leverage GPT4o to generate synthetic QA-pairs based on the gathered information, followed by manual verification to ensure accuracy and relevance. After the synthetic queries are generated by LLM, human annotators can rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure the QA pairs are correct and consistent.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Even the best-performing WebWalker using GPT-4o as its backbone does not surpass 40%, highlighting the challenge posed by WebWalkerQA. WebWalkerQA is built on official websites with dynamically updated information, while pre-trained models rely on static knowledge limited by a cutoff date and lack dynamic updates.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We introduce WebWalkerQA, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs' web traversal abilities in complex, multi-step information-seeking tasks... We evaluate the performance of RAG systems in tackling WebWalkerQA's challenges, specifically, whether they can retrieve deep information.
